title: "Seeing" and "feeling” architecture: how bodily self-consciousness alters architectonic experience and affects the perception of interiors

findings.consequent: Self-report of illusory touch (Q1: 'I was feeling the touch of the stick where I saw the virtual body being touched')
findings.mechanism: Visuo-tactile conflict resolution leading to illusory touch.
findings.quote: synchronous condition scored higher (mean = 2.52, s.e. = 0.18) than the asynchronous condition (mean = −1.10, s.e. = 0.42)

findings.consequent: Self-report of illusory touch causation (Q2: 'I clearly felt that the stick touching the virtual body was causing the touch I was feeling')
findings.mechanism: Visuo-tactile conflict resolution leading to illusory touch.
findings.quote: synchronous condition revealed a higher score (mean = 2.02, s.e. = 0.36) than the asynchronous condition (mean = -0.86, s.e. = 0.46)

findings.consequent: Self-report of self-identification with virtual body (Q3: 'I clearly felt that the virtual body was my body')
findings.mechanism: Visuo-tactile synchrony leading to body ownership illusion.
findings.quote: synchronous condition also showed higher scores (mean = 1.62, s.e. = 0.39) than the asynchronous (mean = 0.62, s.e. = 0.47)

findings.consequent: Self-report on control questions (Q4, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q13, Q14)
findings.mechanism: Lack of specific visuo-tactile modulation for these aspects of experience.
findings.quote: None of the control questions was significantly modulated by factor stroking.

findings.consequent: Self-report of illusory touch with sidewalls (Q7: 'I felt as if the walls of the room were almost lightly touching me')
findings.mechanism: Proximity of walls in peripersonal space leading to embodied sensation.
findings.quote: question 7 to be significantly stronger [t(1, 23) = 3.5973, p = 0.002] in the narrow (mean = −0.73, s.e. = 0.39) as compared to the large room condition (mean = -2.06, s.e. = 0.29).

findings.consequent: Self-report of approaching walls/room retraction (Q12: 'I felt as if the walls were getting closer to myself')
findings.mechanism: Proximity of walls in peripersonal space leading to a feeling of containment.
findings.quote: significantly stronger [t(1, 23) = 3.1759, p = 0.030] in the narrow room (mean = −1.2, s.e. = 0.35) than in the large room (mean = -1.90, s.e. = 0.32).

findings.consequent: Self-report on other questions (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q13, Q14)
findings.mechanism: Lack of specific room-size modulation for these aspects of experience.
findings.quote: No further question was modulated by factor room-size.

findings.consequent: Probability of perceiving bars shorter than reference
findings.mechanism: Fundamental perceptual mechanism for length judgment.
findings.quote: the main factor was the length of the presented bars (beta = -1.154, p < 0.001).

findings.consequent: Probability of perceiving bars shorter than reference
findings.mechanism: Visual scaling of the virtual body within different room proportions.

findings.antecedent: Stroking synchrony x Room size interaction
findings.consequent: Probability of perceiving bars shorter than reference
findings.mechanism: Bodily self-consciousness (induced by stroking) modulates spatial perception, dependent on room size.
findings.quote: the interaction between stroking and room-size were also significant (beta = 0.1017, p = 0.018).

findings.antecedent: Stroking synchrony (synchronous vs. asynchronous) in narrow room
findings.consequent: Probability of perceiving bars shorter than reference
findings.mechanism: Self-identification with virtual body in narrow room improves length estimation.
findings.quote: synchronous narrow room condition was the main driving factor for the interaction (beta = −0.1209, p = 0.049)

findings.antecedent: Stroking synchrony (synchronous vs. asynchronous) in large room
findings.consequent: Probability of perceiving bars shorter than reference
findings.mechanism: Lack of self-identification effect on spatial perception in large, extrapersonal space.
findings.quote: not significant when considered separately (beta = 0.0827, p = 0.170)

findings.antecedent: Stroking synchrony x Room size interaction
findings.consequent: Subjective bar length estimation thresholds (0.75 probability of answering shorter)
findings.mechanism: Bodily self-consciousness (induced by stroking) modulates spatial perception, dependent on room size.
findings.quote: The interaction room-size by stroking was significant [Partial n² = 0.318, F(1, 18) = 8.389, p = 0.01].

findings.antecedent: Stroking synchrony (synchronous vs. asynchronous) in narrow room
findings.consequent: Subjective bar length estimation thresholds (0.75 probability of answering shorter)
findings.mechanism: Self-identification with virtual body in narrow room improves length estimation.
findings.quote: significant differences between synchronous and asynchronous stroking only in the narrow room.

findings.antecedent: Room size (narrow vs. large) under asynchronous stroking
findings.consequent: Subjective bar length estimation thresholds (0.75 probability of answering shorter)
findings.mechanism: Room size affects spatial perception, especially when self-identification is not induced.
findings.quote: differences between the large and the narrow room, but only for asynchronous stroking.

findings.antecedent: Length of horizontal bars on front wall
findings.consequent: Length estimations for horizontal bars on front wall
findings.mechanism: Basic perceptual mechanism for length judgment.
findings.quote: The length of the bars was revealed to be the main factor (p < 0.001).

findings.consequent: Length estimations for horizontal bars on front wall
findings.mechanism: Higher visibility of front wall bars allows direct comparison, reducing influence of bodily self-consciousness.
findings.quote: Stroking and the interaction stroking by room-size were not found to be significant (but revealed a non-significant trend; p = 0.08).

findings.mechanism: General tendency to underestimate length in visually presented environments.
findings.quote: across all conditions participants estimated the bars presented in perspective as shorter than the target line.

findings.antecedent: Self-identification with virtual body (synchronous stroking) in narrow room
findings.mechanism: Self-identification with the virtual body in peripersonal space leads to a more realistic perception of space.
findings.quote: in the narrow room, length estimation significantly improved when participants self-identified with the virtual body (synchronous narrow condition)

stimuli.description: Participants watched their own virtual body (filmed from behind) on an HMD, embedded in a virtual scene representing either a large (6x3.5m) or narrow (6x0.8m) room. Visuo-tactile strokes were applied synchronously or asynchronously to the participant and virtual body.

Images of the large and narrow room interiors with black bars of varying lengths (40-80cm) presented in different positions (front wall, ground, right wall, left wall) for length estimation task. A 50cm vertical bar on the front wall served as reference.

tables.description: 14-item written questionnaire completed after each experimental block, rating subjective experiences on a Likert scale from -3 (not at all) to +3 (very much).

limitations: Subjective feelings of illusory touch with sidewalls and room retraction were weak, despite being statistically significant.
The study used a specific video-based VR setup and stroking method, which may limit generalizability to all architectural experiences.
The length estimation task used static images of bars, not dynamic interaction within the virtual environment.
